rules.name: Dynamic Code Execution (Eval/Exec)
rules.description: Detects the use of functions like eval(), exec(), or getattr() to execute dynamically generated strings, a common zero-day evasion technique.

rules.name: Environment Variable Harvesting
rules.description: The code aggressively iterates over or reads system environment variables, looking for AWS keys, Discord tokens, or other sensitive credentials.

rules.name: Cryptocurrency Wallet Targeting
rules.description: The code searches user directories (like AppData or LocalAppData) for known cryptocurrency wallet files or browser extension profiles.

rules.name: Reverse Shell Initialization
rules.description: The code opens a network socket and redirects standard input/output streams (stdin, stdout, stderr) to that socket, creating a remote interactive shell.

rules.name: Suspicious External Connections
rules.description: The code makes HTTP or socket connections to raw IP addresses, newly registered domains, or services like Pastebin/ngrok used as C2 infrastructure.

rules.name: System Profiling & Fingerprinting
rules.description: The script excessively collects system information (OS version, hostname, MAC address, running processes) before executing its main payload.

rules.name: File Deletion & Cleanup (Defense Evasion)
rules.description: The malware attempts to delete its own files, wipe logs, or clear terminal history immediately after execution to evade forensics.
